title: Day 2 / 500 — ATS-Y1-002 Add Java Runtime Diagnostics
subtitle: Continue from the exact Day 1 repository state.

steps.title: Day 2.1 Verify Day 1 remote SHA and read existing source
steps.why: Start Day 2 by verifying the exact Day 1 handoff and reading the existing application before making changes. The rule for the entire 500-day experience is to extend yesterday's working repository with today's requirement, not rebuild the same files again.

steps.title: Day 2.2 Add non-instantiable RuntimeEnvironmentReport utility
steps.why: Create a small runtime-reporting utility because another developer may see different Java versions between the IDE and terminal. The utility belongs in the existing project and should have one focused responsibility: expose the environment in which the application is actually running.

steps.title: Day 2.3 Read Java runtime and JVM identity from system properties
steps.why: Read the active Java version, runtime, virtual machine, vendor, and operating system from the running process. This turns JDK, runtime, and JVM terminology into something observable during troubleshooting instead of something memorized only for interviews.

steps.title: Day 2.4 Invoke runtime diagnostics from the existing main method
steps.why: Integrate the runtime report into the existing application startup flow. Day 1 behavior stays in place; Day 2 adds only the diagnostic capability required for workstation and environment troubleshooting.

steps.title: Day 2.5 Compile both classes with Java 8 target compatibility
steps.why: Compile the expanded application with the same Java 8 target used on Day 1. The goal is to prove that adding runtime diagnostics has not changed the project's compatibility contract.

steps.title: Day 2.6 Run the application and inspect the active runtime
steps.why: Run the application and inspect the environment information it reports. This demonstrates that the Java version used to execute the program can differ from the class-file target, which is a realistic source of confusion on developer machines.

data.output:
Geospatial Operations Tracking System
Java version: 21.0.11
Java runtime: OpenJDK Runtime Environment
JVM: OpenJDK 64-Bit Server VM
Java vendor: Debian
Operating system: Linux
Application started successfully.

steps.title: Day 2.7 Inspect generated bytecode with javap
steps.why: Inspect the compiled class information and confirm the Java 8 class-file version. Also verify that the application really contains the call to the runtime-reporting utility, connecting the source change to the generated bytecode.

steps.title: Day 2.8 Update question coverage without duplicating Day 1
steps.why: Update question coverage based on what Day 2 actually exercised. New JDK, runtime, and JVM questions can receive primary coverage, while concepts already completed on Day 1 should be recorded only as reinforcement.

steps.title: Day 2.9 Push and verify remote main
steps.why: Push and verify the completed Day 2 state on GitHub. This verified remote commit is the only valid starting point for Day 3 and preserves continuity across the experience.
